s4220: If the direction indicator is missing or not working, may the driver stop giving the hand signal of their intention to manoeuvre immediately before starting the manoeuvre?
s4221: According to paragraph 2 of Article 32 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, before starting a manoeuvre the driver must switch on the direction indicator for the relevant direction, and if there is none or it is not working, give a hand signal. A signal to turn left or make a U-turn is given by the left arm stretched out horizontally to the side, or the right arm stretched out to the side and bent upwards at a right angle at the elbow. A signal to turn right is given by the right arm stretched out horizontally to the side, or the left arm stretched out to the side and bent upwards at a right angle at the elbow. A braking signal is given by raising the left or right arm vertically upwards. A signal with the direction indicator or by hand must be given in good time, before starting the manoeuvre, and must stop immediately after the manoeuvre is completed (a hand signal may stop immediately before the manoeuvre begins). The signal must not mislead other road users. Giving a signal with the direction indicator or by hand does not give the driver priority and does not release them from the duty to take the necessary precautions.
